gaps.new: §48E clean electricity investment credit (Pub. L. 117-169; part of the investment credit under §46(7))
gaps.list: §38(c)(4)(B)(x) specified credits: the §46 credit attributable to the energy credit determined under section 48
gaps.effect: With §48E in the list, tentative minimum tax is treated as zero when capping the credit (§38(c)(4)(A)(ii)(I)), as for the §48 credit it replaces. Without it, a non-corporate holder who owes alternative minimum tax can use no §48E credit that year; it carries back 3 and forward 22 years (§39(a)(4)). Corporations are unaffected (§38(c)(6)(E)). The same Act amended §38(b) and §38(c)(6)(E) and paired §48 with §48E in §6417(b), but left §38(c)(4)(B) alone.
gaps.example: Individual: regular tax 200,000, tentative minimum tax 230,000, 90,000 credit (30% of a 300,000 project). As §48: cap 230,000 - 25% x 175,000 = 186,250, all 90,000 allowed. As §48E: cap 230,000 - 230,000 = 0, none allowed this year.
gaps.dollars: 90,000 of tax deferred. Real cost: nil if the 3 carryback years absorb it; about 16,500 if used 3 years late at 7%; 4,500 to 9,000 if sold under §6418 at an assumed 5-10% discount (best alternative; discount is a market assumption).
gaps.could_cover: Nothing found. No regulation power over the list; §48E(d) borrows §48 rules only for wages, domestic content and progress expenditures; §46 lists the two credits separately. §469 passive credit limits will bind many individuals first.

gaps.new: §414A automatic enrollment requirement for new 401(k) and 403(b) plans (Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023), with exemptions for employers under 3 years old or with 10 or fewer employees
gaps.list: §414(m)(4)(B) and §414(n)(3)(B): requirements for which affiliated service groups are one employer and leased employees are the recipient's employees (§§408(k), 408(p), 410, 411, 415, 416, plus listed paragraphs of §401(a), not §401(k))
gaps.effect: With §414A in the lists, staff of affiliated service organisations and leased employees count toward the 10-employee threshold. Without it, a practice split into a firm plus a management or staffing entity, or one leasing its staff, keeps the sponsor at 10 or fewer and outside the mandate indefinitely. §414(o) anti-avoidance regulations reach only listed requirements. Common-control groups under §414(b)/(c) are probably covered because those apply for purposes of section 401 (#6.40 counted as noise), but not for 403(b) plans.
gaps.example: 12 staff at 60,000, 100% match on the first 3%: automatic enrolment at the 3% minimum costs up to 12 x 1,800 = 21,600 a year in match; if half would enrol anyway, about 10,800 a year avoided.
gaps.dollars: No tax directly; about 10,800 a year of employer match avoided (pre-deduction) in the example. If the reading fails the arrangement is not a qualified cash or deferred arrangement.
gaps.could_cover: §7805(a) regulations (proposed §414A regulations may already aggregate under §414(b), (c), (m), (o): from memory, unverified); the argument that §414A is a §401(k) condition and so within section 401 helps only under §414(b)/(c). Same Act gave §45AA an express aggregation rule in §45AA(f); §414A has none.

other: §38(c)(4)(B) also omits §45Y (successor to the listed §45) and all other 2022 credits (§45U, 45V, 45W, 45X, 45Z, 40B): non-corporate holders in the alternative minimum tax cannot use them that year.

§45AA has no deduction disallowance, unlike sibling §45E(e)(2)(B): the employer gets a 100% credit on up to $300 of contributions per military spouse and still deducts them (about $63 per spouse per year at 21%, 3 years).
§414A(c)(4)(B) small-business exemption has no predecessor-employer rule; (c)(4)(A) has one. §414A has no aggregation rule of its own.
§414(b) and (c) do not name §403, so nothing in the statute aggregates related employers for the §414A(a)(2) 403(b) mandate.
§139L(d)(4) cites a non-existent §265(b)(6)(A)(a)(ii); §265(b)(6)(A)(ii) is evidently meant.
Drafting slips: §45AA(a)(2) and (c) unbalanced parentheses; missing commas in §6103(p)(3)(A) and §6103(l)(13)(F); double comma in §6103(p)(4)(F)(ii); §45E(f)(2)(C) rounding sentence misplaced.
Intended, not gaps: #6.37 (§414(y)(1)(D) has no multi-employer test), #6.65 and #6.69-#6.71 (§6103 disclosures left subject to accounting), #6.78 (§6108(d) internal statistical support).
